promotion_note: DETERMINATION UPDATED 2026-08-06 (nyiso-130): NOT-YET -> CALIBRATED-WITH-CAVEATS. KEEPER UNCHANGED at 2026-08-06-nyiso-128-solar-basis (bundle results/calibration/nyiso128_treatment); no run was promoted, demoted or re-keyed. WHAT CHANGED IS THE LEDGER, NOT THE RESULTS. The C3c-2023 exception nyiso-129 deliberately WITHHELD is now written, under an explicit owner authorization given in session nyiso-130, verbatim: 'After this run if the only outstanding issue is c3c scarcity tail of +12 hours in 2023 I want NYISO registered as calibrated with caveats. C3c is an acceptable gate failure as a ledgered caveat.' The condition is met exactly as stated — C3c is the SOLE non-passing criterion (C1/C2/C3a/C3b/C4/C6/C8 all PASS, C3a +8.8 / +0.8 / -3.2 %) and the 2023 miss is +12 h (22 vs 10). It supplies the IN-TRAINING authorization rule 22's C3c standing rule does not reach (that rule is out-of-training only). TWO DISCIPLINES KEPT: the 2023 entry carries its OWN correctly-signed OVER-production classification and does NOT ride under the inherited 2024 under-production caveat; and nyiso-129's withheld block is PRESERVED as _withheld_exception_history, so the record shows the exception was AUTHORIZED, not quietly widened. Magnitude at full size. Ledgered caveats 1 of 1 (C3c is the only ledgerable criterion under rubric v3.1). THE LANE IS NOT CLOSED AND THIS IS NOT AN EXHAUSTION CLAIM. nyiso-130 IDENTIFIED the over-production's owner and TESTED the fix, which FAILED its own pre-registered kill gate. Identified: 100 % of the model's C3c tail hours in ALL THREE years are Long Island, inside HB14-21, with BOTH Zone-K import paths at their bound — the whole modelled tail forms at the in-window cap on NYC>Long_Island. NYISO publishes (Locality Bulk Power Transmission Capability Report TABLE 1 note 2, identical in the 2024-25, 2025-26 and 2026-27 editions) that the 275/325 MW 'Locality Limit' the cap uses is the transfer limit NET of a 660 MW generation loss-of-source: 'The true N-1-1 Transmission Security Limit is 940 in this scenario, the Bulk Transfer Limit accounts for the loss-of-source of 660 MW.' Tested: arming the published 940 MW (run 2026-08-06-nyiso-130-n11-tsl) collapses the tail to 2 / 0 / 5 h against 10 / 12 / 42 — C3c fails all three years UNDER-produced, 2024 forming ZERO scarcity hours — and fires kill gate K6, the downstate ST_GAS reliability floor taking up the slack (+0.22 / +0.42 / +0.23 TWh forced; share 20.4->22.2 / 22.0->26.0 / 15.4->17.0 %). So Zone-K reliability here is carried by TWO proxies, a too-tight transfer bound and a min_gen floor, and relieving one loads the other. The successor is a JOINT reconciliation of both under rule 19 [R-ONE-MECH], with its own charter and pre-registration — not a bare number swap. Evidence: results/calibration/FINDING-nyiso130-li-transfer-security-limit-2026-08-06.md, PREREG-nyiso130-li-transfer-security-limit-2026-08-06.md, _nyiso130_ab_gates.json, _nyiso130_li_tsl_identification.json. (PRIOR NOTE, nyiso-129 promotion, unedited below.) PROMOTED 2026-08-06 (nyiso-129). NYISO keeper -> 2026-08-06-nyiso-128-solar-basis (bundle results/calibration/nyiso128_treatment), superseding 2026-08-06-nyiso-128-control. THE ESCALATED SOLAR-BASIS TREATMENT IS ADJUDICATED AND PROMOTED, AND IT COSTS A DETERMINATION DOWNGRADE THAT IS CARRIED OPENLY: CALIBRATED-WITH-CAVEATS -> NOT-YET, sole FAIL C3c-2023 (model 22 h vs RT actual 10 h, 2.20x OVER-produced, in-training so the 2026-08-06 C3c standing rule does not reach it). OWNER RULING, session nyiso-129, verbatim: 'Is this a recommended keeper candidate? If so plz promote. If structural integrity improves but gates regress that may still be a keeper.' The session's recommendation was YES on rules 1 [R-STRUCT] / 14 [R-ACCURATE]. WHAT IS ARMED: nyiso_solar_market_generator_basis, a rule 14 input repair with ZERO free parameters (n_residual unchanged at 6) correcting a genuine DOUBLE COUNT — EIA-860's NY utility-scale population carries ~2 GW of distribution-connected NY-Sun community solar that is not a NYISO market generator and is already netted out of the EIA-930 NYIS demand series used as load (NYIS 'NG: SUN' identically zero, 8,760/8,760 h). Capacity basis becomes NYISO's own Gold Book Table III-2a registry (15 units, 573.4 MW). WHAT IT BUYS: C3a PASSES ALL THREE YEARS and improves in the two years that were furthest out — +6.2 / -1.7 / -7.0 % -> +8.8 / +0.8 / -3.2 % (2025 +3.8 pp, 2024 +2.5 pp; 2023 worsens 2.6 pp but stays in band, and the pre-registered adverse case of 2023 crossing +10 % did NOT materialise). C1/C2/C3b/C4/C6/C8 all PASS; scored at HEAD under rubric v3.1. P1 confirmed (JJA h16-h18 2025 CT_PEAKER +109 MW, ST_GAS +365 MW, CC_REGULAR +142 MW against solar -1,218 MW); K5 exonerates the seam (import p50 +52 / 0 / +42 MW), so the removed solar is replaced by IN-STATE THERMAL. WHAT IT COSTS, AND WHY THAT IS RULE 14 WORKING AS WRITTEN: C3c-2023 goes 18 h -> 22 h. nyiso-129 LOCALIZED the regression rather than accepting it as diffuse: all four added hours are Long Island afternoon hours in ONE Sept 2023 heat-wave episode (09-04 16h, 09-07 15h, 09-09 14h/15h; the full 22-hour tail is Aug-21 plus Sept 4-9, every hour Zone K, h14-h19), and Zone K is where the arm removes 97.7 MW of 152.1 MW. Rule 14 states the reading explicitly — a more accurate input that makes the fit worse is a DISCOVERED BUG elsewhere, not a reason to revert: the phantom Zone-K solar was masking an over-tight Long Island representation, which is now the ISO's named successor lever (the queue was EMPTY before this session). The 2023 exception is STILL WITHHELD, not laundered — the miss is an over-production, the opposite sign to the C3c caveat's own classification, so it stands at full magnitude as a FAIL and the determination reads NOT-YET. The ledger budget stays 1 of 3; the ledgered C3c caveat (2024, 0.17x -> 0.25x, still an under-production) is carried forward unchanged in substance. THE nyiso-128b NAMED SUCCESSOR IS REFUTED AS SPECIFIED, ex ante and with no solve spent. That lever was 're-identify the registered fleet's CF from EIA-860 tracking mix + latitude', on the premise that the registered fleet's ~0.20 CF vs the model's 0.133 blend is a geometry difference. MEASURED: the clear-sky POA ratio (registered subset vs whole NY fleet, capacity-weighted tracking mix and centroid latitude, via renewables._clearsky_poa_by_tech) is 1.004 / 1.032 / 1.028 — the two populations sit at the same latitude (42.54 vs 42.69 N) and differ only modestly in tracking share (61 % vs 47 % single-axis), and the registered fleet's DC:AC ratio is LOWER (1.340 vs 1.353). Geometry buys CF 0.133 -> 0.137, so the lever as named is INERT and rule 26 [R-DELETE] forbids parking it. THE REAL OBJECT, newly identified: RENEWABLE_AVG_CF['NYISO']['solar'] = 0.15 is a self-declared Tier-3 approximation carrying 'needs-citation: verify against EIA-923 ISO totals', realized at ~0.133, against a MEASURED 19.5 % for the very fleet this keeper installs (2026 Gold Book Table III-2a per-unit 2025 Net Energy, 981.8 GWh over 573.4 MW, per-unit range 15.8-22.2 %). That is a CF-LEVEL defect on a different input with its own identification, not a geometry correction. Evidence: results/calibration/FINDING-nyiso129-solar-basis-promotion-and-cf-successor-2026-08-06.md, FINDING-nyiso128-market-solar-basis-2026-08-06.md, PREREG-nyiso128-market-solar-basis-2026-08-05.md, _nyiso128_ab_gates.json, _nyiso129_cf_identification.json.

frontier.note: FRONTIER DECLARED + DETERMINATION MOVED NOT-YET -> CALIBRATED-WITH-CAVEATS (owner decision, session nyiso-104: 'I am comfortable with taking c3c as a caveat and calling NYISO calibrated with caveats if we've exhausted options to address scarcity tail'). C3c was the SOLE blocker and every other criterion already PASSED; it is now carried as ONE ledgered caveat (budget 3) via the exceptions block of the keeper's calibration_attestation.json, generated by scripts/gen_nyiso100_attestation.py (the GENERATOR is the source of truth — editing only the emitted JSON is reverted by the next run). THE CAVEAT IS NOT A CLAIM THAT THE BENCHMARK IS WRONG: the measured RT tail is real (model 3/0/7 h vs actual 10/12/42 h >$300) and the model under-produces it. It records an EXHAUSTED lever queue on a diagnosed structural limitation of the five-zone representation — items 1/1b refused ex-ante on identification (nyiso-94/95), item 5 inert ex-ante (nyiso-93), items 2/3 closed and tested (nyiso-96), the last surviving candidate SCUC load-pocket security commitment + BPCG closed ex-ante on CONTENT not merely access (nyiso-97), import shape refused as an attributed C3c symptom with the seam exonerated (nyiso-99), G-J locality refused ex-ante for want of a representable boundary (nyiso-101). The one nominally-open item (nyiso_iroquois_winter_spread) is blocked on a joint SUMMER scarcity lever, and summer is exactly what is exhausted — nyiso-92 dated the actual RT tail as summer (2025 Jun 23-25 alone = 18 of 42 h; the Jan-2024 storm produced ZERO >$300 hours), capping the winter-fuel lane at ~4-5 h/yr. Rule 1 [R-STRUCT] is why this is a ledger entry and not a mechanism: every remaining way to lift the tail is fitted to the tail residual. RE-OPEN CONDITION, satisfiable: a Capital_Hudson -> Zone-F/Zone-G TOPOLOGY SPLIT makes the sub-zonal load pocket representable — its own owner charter (the ERCOT West/Panhandle class, CLOSED), never a mechanism-flag lever. KEEPER UNCHANGED (2026-07-30-nyiso-100-silretire) and NO SOLVE RAN — this is a scorer-side reclassification on the committed bundle. Holdout: NYISO re-declared in the `complete` (VALIDATION-tier) block of calibration-complete.json — 2022 + the 2018/2020/2021 ladder, NOT training; it is deliberately ABSENT from the new `final` (locked-test) block, so 2019 / H1-2026 stay blocked. The ACTIVE holdout spend freeze independently blocks every out-of-training solve regardless, so nothing is spendable until the owner lifts it. Evidence: docs/FINDING-nyiso104-c3c-frontier-and-tiered-holdout-2026-07-31.md.
frontier.amendment_note: THE C3c FRONTIER DECLARATION STANDS, AND ITS PREMISE IS RESTORED. nyiso-108's amendment recorded that the nyiso-104b premise - C3c is the SOLE blocker and every other criterion PASSES - had lapsed, because the hydro input repair exposed a real 2023 fossil over-pricing that failed C3a. nyiso-109 closed that defect on measured grounds (the gas-offer margin anchor resolved per zone, zero free parameters), so C3a PASSES in all three years and C3c is once again the SOLE remaining miss, carried as ONE ledgered caveat. NYISO's determination is CALIBRATED-WITH-CAVEATS. C3c itself is UNCHANGED across this A/B (model 3/0/7 h vs actual 10/12/42 h >$300 in both arms), so no C3c evidence moved, the exhausted-queue finding is untouched, no new caveat slot is spent, and the re-open condition is unchanged: a Capital_Hudson -> Zone-F/Zone-G TOPOLOGY SPLIT under its own owner charter, never a mechanism-flag lever. That defect passes every current gate, so it is not a blocker; it is an open structural item with no lever chartered yet, and it is the named successor lane. Holdout unaffected: NYISO keeps `complete`, stays ABSENT from `final`, and the ACTIVE spend freeze independently blocks every out-of-training solve.
